subject: SIG RFI — asset ownership, retention & data provenance
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@cypherbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: SIG asset ownership and retention clarifications

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking this RFI. A few follow-ups from our SOC 2 / SIG reviewers around data ownership, retention and provenance for requests processed by your hosted inference offering:

1) For inference requests routed through Redwood hosted API, who is the canonical data owner of the request payload and generated model outputs? Is there any access retained by Redwood beyond transient processing?

2) What is your default retention period for request logs, full input payloads, and generated outputs? Is retention configurable per-customer?

3) Key management: do you use a customer-managed KMS option for at-rest encryption of payload caches and logs? If not, what controls protect customer-specific KV caches and prefix caches?

4) Data provenance / auditability: can you produce a sample proof-of-access log showing which internal processes accessed stored request materials and at what time? Our audit team expects deterministic traceability.

5) Deletion / legal holds: how do you implement deletions across caches, backups and analytics pipelines? Typical concern: retained debug telemetry may carry PII.

Please see the attached SIG tab (CypherBank_SIG_RFI_v3.xlsx) with line-item references. We need clarifications by COB Friday to align with procurement review next week.

Appreciate the quick turn —
Liam Carter
Procurement & Security, CypherBank
liam.carter@cypherbank.com

Attachments: CypherBank_SIG_RFI_v3.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@cypherbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: SIG asset ownership and retention clarifications

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear questions and the spreadsheet. Quick summary answers inline — full artifact packet and a short walk-through call would help. Proposed 30-min slot tomorrow afternoon (my calendar attached).

1) Ownership: Customers retain ownership of their input payloads and any generated outputs. Redwood is a processor; we persist only metadata and ephemeral caches needed for serving and performance. We do not assert ownership over customer content.

2) Retention: Default retention for full payloads is 0 days for hosts that opt-in to no-persist. For standard hosted accounts we retain raw input payloads for 7 days (configurable down to 0 or up to 90 days on request). Token-level telemetry is retained 90 days by default; aggregated analytics are kept 2 years. Retention is configurable per-account via the Console or API flag.

3) KMS: We offer both Redwood-managed KMS and a customer-managed KMS (BYOK) option for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted customers we encrypt prefix/KV caches at rest with customer-specific DEKs wrapped by project-level keys. For BYOK customers the DEKs are wrapped by the customer's KMS.

4) Provenance: We can export an access timeline: process id, internal role, service name, timestamp, and justification tag. Sample logs require a short redaction pass; we can provide a redacted extract by EOD Thursday.

5) Deletion/legal hold: Deletion flows cascade: cache eviction, object store purge, analytics ingestion stop, and backup mark-for-delete. Legal holds keep an indelible marker; deletion is paused and tracked with a compliance ticket. We maintain an immutable audit trail of deletion requests with owner and approver metadata.

I'll assemble the artifact packet (access logs sample, KMS manifest, retention config screenshots) and loop Marissa to validate the redaction plan. If Monday is too late for procurement, we'll accelerate.

Available slots for a quick call: Wed 11:00–11:30 or Wed 15:00–15:30 PT. Which works?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
(555) 555-0123

• For retention config screenshots: can you indicate the Console API call or CLI command used to change per-account retention? Our SRE group will want the exact call.

We've attached our procurement checklist so legal can map to internal SLAs. If you can share the sample logs and call/CLI examples before COB Thursday, that'll keep us on schedule.

Liam

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: SIG asset ownership and retention clarifications — artifact packet and samples

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a redacted artifact packet and short answers to the outstanding items. Highlights: 

• BYOK rotation: rotation is customer-controlled via their KMS; Redwood does not perform rotation on behalf of a BYOK customer. For emergency decrypt we have a documented break-glass procedure that requires a multi-person approval and is logged to the immutable incident ledger.

• Access timeline sample: attached redacted CSV contains service (role), truncated actor id, action, and UTC timestamp. We removed any user-identifying fields and truncated object ids to the first 8 chars per our redaction policy.

• Retention CLI example (redwoodctl):
  redwoodctl accounts update-retention --account-id acct-4a7b2c --payload-retention 0d --telemetry-retention 90d
(Also available via the Console > Settings > Data Retention)

• Backups & deletion: backups are marked-for-delete and purged according to backup provider SLA; we provide a compliance ticket and audit trace for legal holds.

Attached files: redwood_kms_key_manifest.csv (redacted), access_timeline_redacted.csv, redwood-sig-artifact-packet-20280323.zip

If you want, we can join a 30-min session to walk the artifact packet tomorrow. Jordan/Karthik — please confirm who will join.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security Assurance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
